// A Lissajous figure: x = XAmplitude * sin(2 * pi * XFrequency * t + Phase),
// y = YAmplitude * sin(2 * pi * YFrequency * t). Closes when the frequency
// ratio is rational; the canonical parameter covers one combined period
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lissajous_curve).
type Lissajous2D
    implements ICurve2D
{
    XAmplitude: Number;
    YAmplitude: Number;
    XFrequency: Number;
    YFrequency: Number;
    Phase: Angle;
}

// The Gielis superformula, a polar shape family covering polygons, stars,
// and organic outlines. Symmetry is the lobe count m; Exponent1..3 are the
// n1, n2, n3 shape exponents; XRadius and YRadius are the a and b scale
// divisors. Closed when Symmetry is a whole number
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superformula).
type Superformula2D
    implements IPolarCurve2D
{
    Symmetry: Number;
    Exponent1: Number;
    Exponent2: Number;
    Exponent3: Number;
    XRadius: Number;
    YRadius: Number;
}

//==
// # Further classical polar curves
//
// Further classical polar curves.
// Every one is a `IPolarCurve2D`, so a single RadiusAt
// body below is the whole implementation: PolarPositionAt / CartesianPositionAt
// / Eval come from `curves.library.plato`.

// The cycloid of Ceva r = Scale * (1 + 2 * cos(2 * theta)): a trisecting
// curve with a single loop inside a larger oval.
// https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommaso_Ceva#The_Cycloid_of_Ceva
type CycloidOfCeva2D
    implements IPolarCurve2D
{
    Scale: Number;
}

// Tschirnhausen's cubic in polar form, r = Scale * sec(theta / 3)^3: a cubic
// with one loop and two branches running to infinity. Undefined where
// theta / 3 reaches a quarter turn.
// https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tschirnhausen_cubic
type TschirnhausenCubic2D
    implements IPolarCurve2D
{
    Scale: Number;
}

// The conchoid of de Sluze r = sec(theta) + Scale * cos(theta): a family whose
// members include the cissoid, the right strophoid, and the trisectrix of
// Maclaurin. Undefined at odd quarter turns.
// https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conchoid_of_de_Sluze
type ConchoidOfDeSluze2D
    implements IPolarCurve2D
{
    Scale: Number;
}

// The sinusoidal spiral r^Exponent = Scale^Exponent * cos(Exponent * theta).
// Exponent selects the member: -1 a line, 1 a circle, 2 the lemniscate,
// -2 a hyperbola, 1/2 a cardioid. Precondition: Exponent is non-zero.
// https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinusoidal_spiral
type SinusoidalSpiral2D
    implements IPolarCurve2D
{
    Scale: Number;
    Exponent: Number;
}

// The trisectrix of Maclaurin in polar form, r = 2 * Scale / cos(theta / 3):
// the classical angle-trisecting cubic.
// https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trisectrix_of_Maclaurin
type TrisectrixOfMaclaurin2D
    implements IPolarCurve2D
{
    Scale: Number;
}

// The transcendental butterfly curve, in canonical position and scaled by
// Scale. Not a polar curve about the origin in the IPolarCurve2D sense: the
// radial factor is paired with the raw parameter angle, so it carries its own
// Eval below. The canonical [0,1] parameter covers the full 12-pi period.
// https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Butterfly_curve_(transcendental)
type ButterflyCurve2D
    implements IClosedCurve2D
{
    Scale: Number;
}

//==
// # Plane spirals, transition curves, and roulettes
//
// The plane curves traced by a steadily growing radius or by a point carried on
// a rolling circle: the classical spirals, the road-and-rail transition curve,
// the gear-tooth involute, and the cycloid family. Each type stores the minimal
// defining parameters; the canonical [0,1] curve parameter maps onto the
// documented sweep or domain, and types without placement fields are defined in
// canonical position. Evaluation lives in `curves-shapes.library.plato`.

//==
// # Spirals and transition curves

// The Archimedean spiral r = StartRadius + GrowthRate * theta (theta in
// radians), swept over Angles: evenly spaced coils
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archimedean_spiral).
type ArchimedeanSpiral2D
    implements IPolarCurve2D
{
    StartRadius: Number;
    GrowthRate: Number;
    Angles: AngleInterval;
}

// The logarithmic (equiangular) spiral r = StartRadius * exp(GrowthRate *
// theta), swept over Angles: self-similar coils, constant crossing angle
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logarithmic_spiral).
type LogarithmicSpiral2D
    implements IPolarCurve2D
{
    StartRadius: Number;
    GrowthRate: Number;
    Angles: AngleInterval;
}

// One branch of Fermat's spiral r = Scale * sqrt(theta), swept over Angles:
// evenly filling coils, the basis of sunflower/phyllotaxis layouts
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermat%27s_spiral).
type FermatSpiral2D
    implements IPolarCurve2D
{
    Scale: Number;
    Angles: AngleInterval;
}

// A clothoid (Euler spiral) arc: curvature grows linearly with arc length,
// kappa(s) = s / (Flatness * Flatness). The parameter is signed arc length s
// over Domain. The standard road and rail transition curve
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler_spiral).
type Clothoid2D
    implements ICurve2D, IArcLengthParameterized<Point2D>
{
    Flatness: Number;
    Domain: NumberInterval;
}
